name: io.github.Tap-Giving/tap-giving-mcp
title: NFC Tap Builder by Tap.Giving
description: Design and order custom NFC tap discs. A person pays the hosted invoice; the server moves no money.

tools.name: get_discovery
tools.description: The orientation response for this server, the design tool NFC Tap Builder by Tap.Giving. It returns the builder's introduction, what the server does (print-ready NFC tap artwork proofs from the published spec and design directions; the artwork is the organization's own, to take to any printer), the product in plain words, the first choice (shape: round or square), the artwork spec summary, and the full capability list with the human gates. Ordering is the optional step after the design path. The response states the access model up front: no account, key, or login at any point; order status is read with the status reference returned at placement. The optional intent argument is echoed back as guidance; a disc count in it is matched with the binding total get_quote returns at that count. Payment stays human: This server moves no money itself: when an order is placed, Tap.Giving emails the invoice and the design proof, and a person pays the hosted invoice. A person pays the invoice when it arrives.

intent.description: Optional free-text description of what the person wants (for example an organization type and a rough disc count). It is echoed back as guidance; a disc count in it points at get_quote for the binding total at that count.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: The binding quote for a prospective order (also known as get_pricing). For a given quantity it returns the tier, the list totals as the headline, and one payable first-order total with the first-order discount scope and its 7-day renewing window explained in plain words, add-ons, free shipping as its own line, the exact grand total, and the turnaround (2 to 3 weeks from artwork approval). No tax line: Tax, where it applies, is calculated on the invoice. Quantities below the 100-disc minimum are refused by this tool itself. It is the tool for the exact price at a named quantity; get_product returns product facts without a quantity, get_order_questions returns the order questions that follow a quote, and the artwork path runs through get_artwork_spec and submit_artwork.

antiMetalCount.description: How many discs go on metal surfaces and need the $1 shielding layer. Omit when unknown (unknown bills nothing). Counts above the quantity are clamped and the clamp is reported.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: The full product facts. Prices are stated in the order phase (get_order_questions, get_quote, get_recap), not here. It returns one block per topic: discs (the locked tap chip, 0.85 mm double-laminated matte waterproof PVC, the 100 mm (4 inch) round and square built-ins; every other size is a manual exception), mounting (options and the metal caveat), stands and badges (table stands and lanyard badges, from the team by email, not ordered through this server), shipping (2 to 3 weeks from artwork approval), samples (there is no sample program; the emailed proof stands in for it), and ordering (tax-exempt, payment, reorder, and design help), plus the Redirect Dashboard and the destination model: per-disc pointing, two destinations, dashboard sign-in timing, and phone compatibility with the printed-code fallback. The optional topic argument returns only one block. It is the tool for product facts alone; get_discovery returns the first orientation, and get_quote returns the price at a quantity.

topic.description: Optional: return only this one product block (discs, stands, badges, mounting, shipping, samples, or ordering), or overview (also general) for the full summary. Omit it to return every block.

tools.name: get_artwork_spec
tools.description: The production artwork spec for the chosen shape: 106 mm artboard, cut, bleed, and safe-zone geometry as structured millimetre data plus plain guidelines, the format wanted back (vector, SVG preferred), delivered example designs to react to (real organizations' finished discs, indexed in full with a bounded set shown inline), labeled explainer photos of discs in place, and the optional logo ask. Artwork is built with the caller's own tools; this server has no design-generation tool. The artwork composed from this spec is the organization's own, vendor-neutral and print-ready to take to any printer. No key is needed. Shape is the first choice (the discovery response names it as such, and get_discovery returns the orientation when no shape has been chosen yet); the shape argument selects round or square geometry, and submit_artwork is the tool that accepts the finished artwork file. chosenExampleRef carries the delivered example the person picked, from the examples this tool returns.

shape.description: The disc shape to return geometry for: round or square. Omit it to return both shapes.

chosenExampleRef.description: The delivered example the person picked: its pick-list number for the chosen shape, any example id from the structured examples index, or the example's description words. It is carried with the spec as the design reference.

tools.name: get_examples
tools.description: The finished discs: the real designs Tap.Giving produced and delivered to organizations, returned as labeled images, paged nine at a time, round first then square. Each example is labeled with its shape and pick number (the same numbers get_artwork_spec prints and accepts as chosenExampleRef), its description, and the organization it was delivered to. The shape argument filters by shape, and offset pages the full set; the structured content names the totals by shape and the next page's offset when more remain. It is the tool that returns examples or finished work at any point in the journey; get_artwork_spec returns the spec for designing from a picked direction. No key is needed.

shape.description: Optional: only this shape's delivered designs, or all of them (round first, then square). Defaults to all.

offset.description: Optional: how many examples to skip before this page. Defaults to 0; the answer's nextOffset names the next page's offset when more remain.

count.description: Optional: how many examples to show on this page, at most 9. Defaults to 9.

tools.name: submit_artwork
tools.description: The finished-artwork intake: it accepts a completed artwork file and returns the design composited on the disc as a proof. The artwork stays the organization's own: print-ready and vendor-neutral, theirs to take to any printer; submitting it obliges no order. Intake is permissive by ruling: a real image is accepted in any format and rejected only on three sanity grounds (malicious or masquerading content, over 5 MB decoded, or not decodable as the type it claims). Production fitness is judged later in the normal proof flow, never here. No email is needed on the cold path. The optional designUrl argument records the destination the design was built for (mid-to-late design phase); the optional chosenExampleRef names the delivered example the design follows, and its reproduction data rides the answer beside the verify-against-example checklist. The file argument carries the artwork file (filename, mediaType, contentBase64); sha256 is the hex SHA-256 of those file bytes; shape optionally names the shape the artwork was designed for; orderRef optionally attaches the submission to an existing order; logo optionally carries the source logo the artwork was built from; note is free text for the team. Each call creates a separate submission: resubmitting the same file mints a new artworkRef rather than replacing the earlier one. It returns the artworkRef every later step carries, a displayUrl, and a preview of the person's own design composited on the disc (cut shape applied) for the renderable formats (SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF); for a format this server cannot render here (for example PDF), the answer says so plainly and never promises a preview or an email at this stage. Design approval stays human: a person approves the final proof by email before production. No tool on this server records or implies an approval.

file.description: The artwork file itself: its filename, its media type, and its bytes as base64.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the file bytes.

shape.description: Optional: the shape the artwork was designed for; the on-disc preview uses its cut. Omit it and the preview shows both shapes.

orderRef.description: Optional: attach the submission to an order already created (the orderRef create_order returned).

logo.description: Optional source logo the artwork was built from; travels with the submission as source material.

note.description: Optional free-text note for the Tap.Giving team, carried with the submission.

designUrl.description: Optional: the URL the disc should open, entered in the design phase. The design QR code is a labeled mock built from it; production encodes the disc's Redirect Dashboard link to this same destination, and the recap confirms it.

chosenExampleRef.description: Optional: the delivered example this design follows (its pick-list number, an example id, or the example's description words); its reproduction data rides the answer.

tools.name: start_order_intent
tools.description: An optional step on the order path, not the start of the journey: it captures a contact email through the same public capture endpoint the website's email-first door uses, so follow-up rides the existing lead machinery. No key is needed. An intent is a lead, not an order: it creates no invoice and reserves nothing. It returns an intentRef, links an artworkRef when given, and says plainly what follow-up to expect. The email must be a real, reachable address: reserved domain endings (.example, .test, .invalid) and the example domains are refused, because no follow-up could ever reach them. Placing an order needs no key. One intent per email: a repeat call with the same email returns the existing intentRef and creates no second lead. This tool captures the contact only; create_order is the later tool that sets up the order itself, and it needs no key either.

email.description: The contact email to capture; follow-up goes to this address.

quantityHint.description: Optional rough disc count the person mentioned; it shapes the follow-up and is not a binding quote.

artworkRef.description: Optional: link an earlier submit_artwork reference to this intent.

sourceNote.description: Optional free-text note about where this contact came from or what they asked about; it travels with the lead for the team.

tools.name: get_order_questions
tools.description: The order questions as structured data, returned in the exact order they are asked: the contact email first (captured through start_order_intent), then the organization name, the shipping address and phone, quantity, shape, the metal count, mounting with the picture assets, the artwork answer (artwork already in hand, or the team designs it from the organization name), and the link destination as a confirmation of the destination carried from the design. The contact name and phone ride create_order. Prices are first stated here, in the order phase: the price range and the no-fees line ride this answer. It is the tool for the point where a person is ready to order; get_discovery returns the first orientation.

tools.name: get_recap
tools.description: The full recap, the last thing before the exits: it validates the same order inputs create_order will carry (quantity from 100 to 7000, one of the two built-in sizes, adhesive or screws mounting, a complete shipping address) and returns the submitted artwork (displayUrl plus image content where renderable), the quantity, the shipping address as entered, the exact cost from get_quote, and both required notes. It returns a recapRef; create_order carries it, and an order whose inputs differ from the recap is refused as a conflict. The contactEmail argument (the email captured with start_order_intent) and the artworkRef argument (the reference submit_artwork returned, when a design was submitted) bind the recap to the flow. Without a contactEmail the same complete summary returns as an unbound summary, marked not placeable; an unbound recap asserts nothing about what the flow captured elsewhere, and create_order refuses it. No key is needed.

quantity.description: Discs in the order, 100 to 7000; priced from the published tiers.

size.description: The built-in size and shape: 100mm-round or 100mm-square.

mounting.description: How the discs mount: adhesive backing, or pre-drilled screw holes plus adhesive.

antiMetalCount.description: How many discs sit on metal surfaces and need the $1 shielding layer. Omit when unknown; an unknown count bills nothing.

shipTo.description: The shipping address for the finished discs; every field is required, and the phone is its own field.

name.description: Recipient name or organization name at the shipping address.

phone.description: A phone number for the delivery address.

artworkRef.description: Optional: the artwork reference submit_artwork returned; pass it so the submitted design shows on the disc in the recap. Without it, the recap cannot show a design the flow submitted.

linkDestination.description: Optional: the page a tap opens. Any http or https URL, changeable anytime; the Redirect Dashboard is the default.

contactEmail.description: The order contact email: pass the email captured with start_order_intent; it binds the recap for placement. The final proof is emailed there, so it must be an address the organization owns.

contactName.description: Optional display only: the contact person's name, echoed in the recap.

contactPhone.description: Optional display only: the contact phone, echoed in the recap.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: The final step of the order path, labeled "Email me my invoice and design proof." It sets up an order through the same front door a website order takes (an INVREQ record the hourly adoption resolves into the CRM, indistinguishable downstream). This is the lock-in write behind both recap exits; it carries the recapRef and a required idempotencyKey (a retry with the same key and payload returns the original orderRef; the same key with a different payload is a conflict naming the differing fields). The 100-disc minimum is enforced here. Sizes other than the two built-ins return manual_exception. It returns the orderRef (the reference every later call uses), the exact quote, the chosen exit, and the next step. Failure modes: a recap whose inputs differ from the order is refused as a conflict naming the differing fields; a reused idempotencyKey with a different payload is a conflict naming the original order. The order's inputs are the same inputs get_recap validated for its recap (start_order_intent is the earlier contact capture); the recapRef binds the order to that recap. Placing the order records it, emails the full order to the Tap.Giving team, creates the invoice at the quoted total, and emails the invoice and the design proof to the contact; the response carries each step's outcome, the settled confirmation text, and the order's status reference. Your reference is in your invoice email; if you cannot find it, email hello@tap.giving from the order email and the team re-sends it. A replay with the same idempotencyKey re-attempts only the steps that did not complete. Design approval stays human: a person approves the final proof by email before production. No tool on this server records or implies an approval. Payment stays human: This server moves no money itself: when an order is placed, Tap.Giving emails the invoice and the design proof, and a person pays the hosted invoice. A person pays the invoice when it arrives.

contactName.description: The contact person's name for the order.

contactEmail.description: The order contact email; the final proof is emailed there, so it must be an address the organization owns.

contactPhone.description: A phone number that reaches the contact.

size.description: 100mm-round or 100mm-square; anything else is a manual exception handled by hand through the Tap.Giving team.

mounting.description: How the discs mount: adhesive backing, or pre-drilled screw holes plus adhesive.

antiMetalCount.description: How many discs sit on metal surfaces and need the $1 shielding layer. Omit when unknown.

shipTo.description: The shipping address for the finished discs; every field is required.

name.description: Recipient name or organization name at the shipping address.

phone.description: A phone number for the delivery address.

linkDestination.description: Any http or https URL; optional, changeable anytime; the Redirect Dashboard is the default.

artworkRef.description: The artwork reference submit_artwork returned for this order's design.

note.description: Optional free-text note carried on the order for the team.

recapRef.description: The reference get_recap returned for these same inputs; the order is refused if its inputs differ from that recap.

exit.description: The person's chosen exit, recorded on the order. Both exits write the same record shape.

idempotencyKey.description: 8 to 128 characters, minted per intended order, reused on retries.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Where an order stands, read with the order's status reference: the capability create_order returned once at placement (also carried in the customer email). No account or login exists; the reference itself is the credential, and an unknown reference answers not_found. It returns the tightened exposure set: the stage, the fulfillment state with tracking when present, the invoice state with its hosted link, the quantity, shape, and mounting, the order's own artwork preview, and the Redirect Dashboard block. It never returns the full business record, a shipping phone, or internal record ids. An order not yet adopted returns stage "received" with the adoption expectation, not an error. It is the read for an existing order and never changes anything; get_recap covers the period before an order exists, and get_order_questions returns an order's inputs.

statusRef.description: The status reference create_order returned at placement. It is also carried in the invoice email; if it cannot be found, email hello@tap.giving from the order email and the team re-sends it.
